tip_title: The Holidays Are Coming. Your Home Policy Has a Personal Property Limit Worth Knowing Before You Start Shopping.
topic: Home Insurance - Holiday and End-of-Year Personal Property Coverage Review
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: The Holidays Are Coming. Your Home Policy Has a Personal Property Limit Worth Knowing Before You Start Shopping.**

October is when the big gift-buying season actually starts — and a lot of people don't realize their homeowners or renters policy has a personal property limit that hasn't been updated since they first bought the policy. If you're adding jewelry, electronics, instruments, or other high-value items over the next couple of months, the standard coverage amount may not be enough to replace them if something goes wrong. The same goes for gifts sitting in your home before you give them away. Most standard policies also have sub-limits for specific categories like jewelry and collectibles that are well below the full personal property limit, so a $5,000 ring doesn't automatically get $5,000 in coverage even if your total limit sounds plenty high.

Not sure where your limits land or whether your most valuable stuff is fully covered? Your Peachy agent can pull up your declarations page and walk through it with you before the season kicks off.

📖 [Learn more from NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/insurance/home-inventory-insurance)
summary: Covers personal property coverage limits and sub-limits on homeowners and renters policies framed as a pre-holiday action item, specifically addressing whether high-value gift purchases and existing valuables are adequately covered before the buying season begins.
scoring_notes: Works across all three audiences — East Cobb (78% homeowners, high income, active holiday buyers), Perimeter (55% homeowners plus renter population covered by renters policy angle), and Lewisville Lake (65% homeowners, family-heavy with gift-heavy holiday season). October timing is ideal — early enough to act before holiday shopping peaks. Personal property sub-limits have not been covered as a standalone topic from this angle in the last 6 months. Prior home inventory tips covered documentation and valuation methods; this tip is framed around coverage adequacy at a specific seasonal trigger point. The home inventory topic has been covered before but from the documentation/tool angle, not the coverage-limit-check angle at holiday season.
